items.note: N1 states the lemma faithfully (y_S += x_S for arbitrary scratch; forward/inverse/forward gives (-Y,X) and restores scratch), and the method follows the schedule logic and three-stage composition (lines 741-763). But the plan never says what the network is built on (three-element subsets, the neighbour rules) or gives the central coefficients |S∩T| mod 2 and (|S∩T|-1)/2 (lines 752-758). Those coefficients are why the net map is the identity, so I judged the derivation partial, the conservative choice.

States D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} with edge operators D_v D_u^{-1}. Derives it from the stored-equals-frame-applied-to-logical invariant and the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise linear gate, exactly as at lines 804-817. The route sign epsilon_w is not mentioned.

N3.1 states the decreasing-edge lemma correctly (line 998) and N3.2 gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 (lines 1105-1110). The identities L=Ich and sum|Δdim|=Wm-2N+2L are never given; the plan only says the total is 'below Wm'. The method also omits two things the count rests on: the bilinear form that makes neighbouring triple lines orthogonal (lines 856-870) and the telescoping signed sum (lines 1066-1071).

Statement matches Prop. bit-motif-interface: projection matrices, endpoint difference I_m, and s_b<W_b m with deficit N-2L_b. The method says every edge difference is a residual projection whose rank is the dimension change. It leaves out the N exceptional first edges on X_a, matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one where the dimension change is zero (lines 1162-1165). Those edges account for the -N rather than -2N in s_b, so the derivation is partial.

The route matches lines 1231-1315: weight additive mod 4 on orthogonal vectors, odd-weight unit vectors giving one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) each, s_c factors on k columns, the Z-correction C=iZC^{-1}Z on the 27k inverse factors, and undoing the exchange. The statement calls the frames 'phase frames i^{wt(P_U x) mod 4}' and drops the H^{⊗m}…H^{⊗m} conjugation of line 1193, which is what turns the phase into a translation kernel.

The plan states s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m, L/N<1/2, and that the deficits exceed 20·2^{-50}, which gives s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}. It does not give the exact eta_b and eta_c (lines 1319-1325) or the log m<20 exponential estimate (lines 1332-1338) that turns the deficit into the exponent. So the item is stated rather than derived.

Lists the elementary operations and the controlled shift and unit scaling, each costing O(V). Proves them by aligned digit splits, the cyclic row split, the cut-and-re-merge at Q-a, and the increasing-piece split for unit multiplication, as at lines 513-527 and 574-604. Negation is not mentioned.

Both lemmas are stated correctly and derived along the paper's route: topmost-row/rightmost-pivot elimination, then triangular factors applied as controlled shifts, then each pivot done as two controlled shifts around one interchange. The choice of a fixed odd prime q avoiding the denominators (lines 1413-1423) is not mentioned.

The steps reproduce the proof of the proposition: cyclic row split into W role streams, Phi_{A_e} on each edge by recursive interchanges, endpoint matrices giving H<-H+D, the three-update interchange, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with its geometric sum, and the fixed-tape parking-stack schedule at O(V) per node.

The steps follow the proof of lem:chunk-swap: the top rho digits become a row field R>=W^k, rows are padded to a multiple of W^k, the remaining width is split in base m with a power-width call per piece (geometric sum), the high-digit moves are reversed, and binary ranges are padded to [q^e].

The route is the paper's: conjugate by P_M, use elementary row additions for M, get inverse children from forward ones via Z conjugation, total s_c children on e/m axes, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. L1 says 'the f-fold forward child on each of the s_c residual-basis slots', but there are only m slots. Per edge, the children run on slots 1..rho_edge, and s_c is the total over the network (lines 1878-1882, 1904-1906).

Follows the proof: eight packed rotations, each done by swap, controlled shift and swap back. The bad set from guards outside [10,2^{K-1}-11] has fraction at most 80(f-1)2^{-K} by the union bound; it is repaired by extraction and stable radix sort, and the top position gets a two-bit XOR. The cost is O(V(L^tau+1)) in the parameter family. One small misdescription of the cycle composition is listed under errors.

The node overhead, row source, u=Wg+w split and recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) are correct. L2.3 says the recurrence sums to O(e^lambda) and drops the leaf contribution O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) (lines 2421-2430). It also omits the bound K<=e^{c/beta} at internal nodes (lines 2413-2415) and never states the condition lambda'>max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}.

States the O(Vd^{lambda'}) layer that is exact up to one truncation with error below sqrt2·2^{-p}. Derives it from the phase-frame recursion and row split, the guard width Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) from A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits, epsilon·C_1<1, and the unit row sums of H. This matches lines 2450-2586 and 2686-2758.

All three parts follow the paper. Character cancellation uses the shift by t/2^{v+1}. Decimation in frequency stores the output in bit-reversed order and the reversed procedure gives F^+B^{-1}. The layout L (prefix slots, then at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges) leads to cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+ell d^{lambda'}]) and error sqrt2·ell·2^{-p}, using the commutation of truncation with J_E.

The proof steps (evaluation at B_0=2^{4p} in 4pr bits, four multiplier products, centered residues with |h_j|<B_0/2, negacyclic reduction) match lines 3233-3368. The statement never says the output is the normalized Q_p(fg/r): it omits the division by r.

States M_r=(f*g)/T with error sqrt2·M(3ell+1)2^{-p} and the stated cost. The derivation follows the proof: keep the LB order, which commutes with pointwise products; take signed-packed products, apply the opposite transform, scale exactly by M, and total the 3delta+eta errors. The normalization identity F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) is only implicit.

The one-dimensional identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, the HvdH maps, ||N-I||<1/2 and the left inverse D N^{-1} C all match lines 3576-3642. So do the tensor identity, the linewise padding, the O(d^2) axis exposure at O(Tp(1+ell^tau)) each, and the count of at most 2dT/r lines.

Both identities are stated exactly. The proofs follow the paper: compare the coefficient of u_k for the chirp, use F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+, commute R with pointwise products, and apply the normalized convolution rule. The conjugation clause appears in A7.2.

The fixed rationals, sizes, alpha, gamma=o(b), prime intervals, gcd, T/2<S<T, separation, trial-division search and no-wrap digit polynomials with coefficients below 2^{3b} all match the paper. eta=1/(4d) is only implied by the condition log x>8d.

Steps follow the paper: the algebra isomorphism with mu_i=P_i^{-1}, triangular updates from i=d down to 1 as prefix-controlled rotations of the valid interval, and O(d^2) chunk interchanges, for cost O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)). The explicit formula b_i=a_i+mu_i·sum_{j<i}a_jP_j is described but not displayed.

The well-definedness, diagonal isomorphism and wrap computation match lines 4303-4319, and A6.1 describes the computed twist, ring convolution and untwist with 2·2^{-p} twist arrays. The normalized identity M_C(f,g)=D_-ι^{-1}M_r(ιD_+f,ιD_+g)=(f*g)/T is never stated.
The source transform (A, then chirp, then B_0, then 2^gamma, with exact counterpart RF_s and the opposite by conjugation) and the six-step algorithm with its two S scalings are as at lines 4456-4544.

The error chain matches the paper: contraction and bilinear error propagation, chirp error <8TL, source error 9·2^gamma·TL, opposite error (3E_s+2), final error <448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2, and carries below Q_0^2 with the invariant. E_ring and E_w are not given numerically, but the chain is the paper's.

The normalization by Tp, the margins with min g_i=g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, the log-power absorption and the schoolbook cutoff are as in the paper. The seven normalized terms are never listed. The argument that setup, per-record or per-line work and exceptional-address sorting are o(V) (lines 4913-4981) is absent.
The root only lists nlogn-conjecture under 'relies on'. No step states the eventual-lower-bound or liminf argument.

errors.says: The labels must keep the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to the number of data banks.
errors.paper: The loss must be small relative to N (L<N/2), the number of addresses per bank (N=v^3). There are only two data banks.

errors.says: Edge differences are projections onto residuals, whose rank is the dimension change.
errors.paper: The N first edges on X_a are exceptions: matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one where the dimension change is zero. This is why s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b rather than W_b m-2N+2L_b.
The frame is C_U=H^{⊗m} diag(i^{q_U(x)}) H^{⊗m}. The Hadamard conjugation turns the character (-1)^{v·x} into the translation X_v.

errors.says: Rows are dealt cyclically into W role streams, with the row count padded per prefix to a multiple of W.
errors.paper: In the power-width proposition the row field is assumed divisible by W^k, and there is no padding there. Padding to a multiple of W^k is done by the callers (chunk-swap and layer).

errors.says: Apply the f-fold forward child on each of the s_c residual-basis slots.
errors.paper: A group has m slots. For each edge, children act on slots 1..rho_edge, and s_c is the total number of child calls over the whole network.

errors.says: Compose two three-cycles on the parity pairs (u,w) into a transposition.
errors.paper: The composition is (00 10)(01 11), a product of two transpositions that flips the parity of u.

errors.says: The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) sums to O(e^lambda).
errors.paper: Only the internal costs sum to O(e^lambda). The leaves add O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), which is why lambda' must exceed sigma+beta(1-sigma).

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. It goes from the two networks to the chunk interchange and the simultaneous layer, then synthetic transforms and convolution, Gaussian resampling with the chirp and permutation cancellation, the six-step algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table. It thins out in three places. The network counts give no L=Ich or Wm-2N+2L identity, omit the source-projection exception in s_b, and skip the explicit eta and log m<20 step that fixes tau. The layer recurrence drops the leaf term behind the lambda' condition. The time accounting lists neither the seven terms nor the o(V) setup and repair argument.
